main_theorems.label: Theorem 1.1 (thm:main, 'The rational-two-torsion 2-converse')
main_theorems.statement: Verbatim (TeX transliterated): 'Let E/Q be an elliptic curve with E(Q)[2] != 0 and s_2(E) in {0,1}. Then ord_{s=1} L(E,s) = rank_Z E(Q) = s_2(E), Sha(E/Q) is finite.' Here s_2(E) = corank_{Z_2} Sel_{2^infty}(E/Q) with the usual local Kummer conditions (introduction.tex lines 16-19). Intro adds: 'The statement includes one rational two-torsion line and full rational two-torsion, CM and non-CM curves, every rational isogeny configuration, and every reduction type at 2 and at the bad primes. ... It does not assert the full Birch--Swinnerton-Dyer leading-coefficient formula, nor does a bound rank E(Q)<=1 alone imply its Selmer hypothesis.' (lines 32-37).
main_theorems.hypotheses: (1) E/Q elliptic curve (modular by BCDT); (2) E(Q)[2] != 0, i.e. E[2] is an extension of two trivial F_2-modules; (3) s_2(E) := corank_{Z_2} Sel_{2^infty}(E/Q) in {0,1}. No hypothesis on reduction at 2 or at bad primes, on CM, or on residual image. Conclusion is only rank equality and finiteness of Sha; NOT the BSD formula and NOT any bound on #Sha.

main_theorems.label: Proposition 9.14 (pw:odd-base, 'Odd original base') - corank-one half of the main theorem
main_theorems.hypotheses: E(Q)[2] != 0; s_2(E)=1. Proof: parity gives odd sign; choose a fixed negative discriminant k with L(E^{(k)},1) != 0, K=Q(sqrt k) split at 2N (Heegner hypothesis), nonexceptional; s_2(E/K)=1 by the quadratic corank identity; build binary families of twists h_x (all primes split in K) with E^{(h_x)} of analytic order 1 and E^{(h_x k)} of analytic order 0 with uniformly bounded normalized Heegner index; apply Thm 4.2 (fixed-K ring-class missing-vertex transfer).

If a(A) in {0,1}, then r(A)=a(A) and the whole group Sha(A/Q) is finite. In that case s_2(A)=a(A).' Lemma 2.2 verbatim: 'For every elliptic curve A/Q, (-1)^{s_2(A)} = epsilon(A). general_results.label: Theorem 3.1 (cy:lower-bound, 'Cyclotomic lower bound')
general_results.statement: Verbatim: 'There is a constant C_E such that, for every allowed h with L(E^{(h)},1) != 0, v_2(L(h)) >= 2w(h)+s(h)-C_E. The constant is independent of the number and sizes of the primes dividing h.' Here L(h)=sqrt|h| L(E^{(h)},1)/Omega_E^{sgn h}, t_q=dim_{F_2}E[2]^{Fr_q}, 2w(h)=sum_{q|h} t_q, s(h)=length_{Z_2} Sha(E^{(h)}/Q)[2^infty] (cyclotomic.tex 14-28).
general_results.hypotheses: E/Q fixed with E[2] an extension of two trivial F_2-modules (E(Q)[2] != 0); h a product of distinct signed primes q*=(-1/q)q with q not dividing 2N, with fixed sign and fixed local squareclasses at 2N; L(E^{(h)},1) != 0 (so s(h) finite by GZK). C_E is NOT effective (built from Kato's fixed-form lattice index c_E, unsmoothing, local twisting classes at 2N, Poitou-Tate real terms).
general_results.location: sections/cyclotomic.tex lines 35-43 (statement), proof lines 752-761; machinery: Kato classes at p=2 (cyclotomic.tex 313-421), rational divisibility via Kato Thm 12.5(3) (423-595), Prop 3.7 central determinant formula (629-748)
general_results.relevance: #Sha(E^{-7}) only in principle: h=-7 is an allowed discriminant (7 not dividing N, (-1/7)7=-7), so it would give v_2(L_*(-7)) >= t_7 + length Sha(E^{-7}/Q)[2^infty] - C_E, i.e. an upper bound on the 2-part of Sha(E^{-7}) by v_2 of the normalized L-value plus an unknown constant. Since C_E is ineffective, it yields nothing computable. No content at odd p. Does not address FIN/ORDER9/Q36.

general_results.label: Theorem 3.2 (cy:missing-vertex, 'Transfer to the missing vertex')
general_results.statement: Verbatim: 'Let h_0 be an allowed discriminant with s_2(E^{(h_0)})=0. Suppose that for arbitrarily large b there are a finite set Q of distinct primes q not dividing 2Nh_0 and linear forms lambda_q: F_2^b -> F_2 giving h_x = h_0 prod_{q in Q}(q*)^{lambda_q(x)}, x in F_2^b, all in the fixed local and sign classes. Suppose that a number B, independent of the family, satisfies L(E^{(h_x)},1) != 0, D(h_x) <= B (x != 0). Then L(E^{(h_0)},1) != 0 and D(h_0) <= B+C_E.' with D(h)=v_2(L(h))-2w(h)-s(h).
general_results.hypotheses: E(Q)[2] != 0; base twist h_0 with 2^infty-Selmer corank ZERO; existence of binary families with uniform bound B. Proof: uniform integrality 2^{C_int} u in Lambda[G] (cy:uniform-integrality), Prop 3.7, and Lemma 3.4 (binary congruences / Chevalley-Warning).
general_results.relevance: none: requires a corank-0 base. For E (s_2=2) inapplicable (K-RANK2). For E^{-7} as base the conclusion L(E^{-7},1) != 0 is already PROVED_COMPUTER_ASSISTED.

general_results.label: Proposition 3.7 (cy:central, 'Central determinant formula')
general_results.statement: Verbatim: 'There is a constant C_loc, depending only on the fixed curve and local classes, with the following property. If s_2(E^{(h_x)})=0, then u_x(0)=0 when L(E^{(h_x)},1)=0. Otherwise |v_2(u_x(0)) - D(h_x)| <= C_loc. The rational positive complex at t=0 has cohomology only in degree one, of dimension two, so these are specializations of the same determinant.' The proof contains an integral Poitou-Tate length identity (cy:pt-length): length H^2(G_{Q,S},T_h) = s(h_x) - i + sum_{q in S} length H^0(Q_q,A_h) + O_E(1), with integral Kummer conditions at every place and 'No unramified condition replaces the Kummer condition at a bad prime.'
general_results.hypotheses: E(Q)[2] != 0; s_2(E^{(h_x)})=0; Kato zeta class of the fixed form; Nekovar Thm 6.3.4 / Sec 6.9.1 / 5.7.1.6 for Poitou-Tate with real Tate-cochain convention.
general_results.relevance: none (corank-0 only; 2-adic only). Note for the record: it is a 2-adic 'Kato divisibility + control' computation that explicitly handles additive reduction at 2 via a small formal subgroup; no analogue is offered at odd p.

general_results.label: Lemma 4.5 (rl:kummer, 'Integral Kummer local condition')
general_results.statement: Verbatim: 'Let F be a finite extension of a nonarchimedean local field of characteristic zero, and let B/F be any elliptic curve. Put M_F = B(F)^_2 = lim B(F)/2^n B(F). There is a perfect local condition U_F = M_F[-1] -> RGamma(F,T_2B). For every n>=1, derived reduction has H^0(U_F (x)^L Z/2^n) = B(F)[2^n], H^1(U_F (x)^L Z/2^n) = B(F)/2^n B(F). ... The condition is its own exact orthogonal complement under local Tate duality. These assertions hold at F|2, for all reduction types, and without a condition on B[2].'
general_results.hypotheses: Any elliptic curve over any p-adic field; uses Milne ADT I Thm 3.2/Cor 3.4 and Nekovar Prop 5.2.4.

general_results.label: Proposition 4.6 (rl:characters, 'Finite-precision ring-class characters')
general_results.statement: Verbatim: 'Fix finitely many split primes of K above odd rational primes, outside 2N, and orient one prime in each conjugate pair. There are distinct split rational primes r_i avoiding all the fixed data and characters xi_i: Gal(H_{r_i}/K) -> Z/2^{n_i}Z, n_i -> infinity, such that xi_i is surjective on the inertia quotient at r_i, is zero at the primes above 2N, and has odd value at each prescribed oriented prime. We can require r_i -> 1 in Z_2 and v_2(2+a_{r_i}(E)), v_2(2-a_{r_i}(E)), v_2 det(1 +- Fr_{r_i} | T) <= c_E. The constant c_E is independent of the list and of K.'
general_results.hypotheses: E/Q any (non-CM: Serre open image; CM: Serre 1968 Cartan image); K imaginary quadratic, not an extra-unit field, not the CM field. 2-adic only.

general_results.label: Lemma 5.2 (rd:derivative, 'Descent and the switch at 2') with Lemma 5.1 (rd:local-model)
general_results.statement: Verbatim: 'There is one integer L != 0, depending on the fixed curve, parametrization and fixed local types, such that the classes obtained from the Heegner derivatives of L times the point satisfy, for every finite switched set I, P_I in H^1(C_I), f(P_{I cup {l}})=0, s(P_{I cup {l}}) = J f(P_I). The same L works for every number of active and derivative primes.' Proof uses Kolyvagin derivative operators D_l = sum i sigma_l^i at inert primes l with Fr_l -> complex conjugation, integral descent killed by a fixed scalar 2^e (Bogomolov homothety), and states 'No good-ordinary or semistability condition was used.' and 'The displayed local formulas agree with the calculation underlying [Howard, Prop 1.7.4]; Howard's odd-prime global hypotheses are not being asserted at 2.'
general_results.hypotheses: E/Q; K=Q(sqrt k) imaginary quadratic satisfying the split Heegner hypothesis at 2N (every prime of 2N splits in K), not an extra-unit field, not the CM field; h a product of signed good odd primes split in K; derivative primes inert in K; p=2 only.
general_results.relevance: none for the seed. It is a 2-adic Kolyvagin-system construction for reducible E[2]; the seed's Sha[2^infty]=0 is known. The seed's K=Q(sqrt-7) violates the Heegner hypothesis required here (3, 2243, 5843 are inert in K), so none of the ring-class machinery of Sections 4-5 accepts the lab's K.

general_results.label: Corollary 4.1 (rd:ring-lower, 'Ring-class lower bound')
general_results.statement: Verbatim: 'Every simple-zero ring instance in the stated data satisfies 2j_h >= 4w(h)+s(h)+s(hk)-C(E,A), omega(k) <= A.' Here j_h is the 2-adic index valuation of the primitive weighted Heegner sum P_h = sum_{sigma in Gal(H_{|h|}/K)} chi_h(sigma) sigma(y_{|h|}) in the free rank-one lattice E^{(h)}(K)^_2/torsion; s(h), s(hk) the Sha[2^infty] lengths of the two rational twists. Uniform form restated as Prop 9.1(2) (pointwise.tex 51-59).
general_results.hypotheses: E(Q)[2] != 0; K=Q(sqrt k) imaginary, split at 2N (Heegner), not extra-unit, not CM field, omega(k) <= A; h product of distinct signed good odd primes split in K, (h,k)=1; L(E^{(h)},s)L(E^{(hk)},s) has a SIMPLE zero at s=1 (so by Gross-Zagier/Kolyvagin both twists have finite Sha). C(E,A) ineffective (ultraproduct argument, Prop 5.7).
general_results.location: sections/ring-limits.tex lines 42-50 (statement); proof ring-determinants.tex 1193-1203 via Prop 5.5 (rd:away-two, 617-707), Prop 5.7 (rd:outer-bound, 745-881), Prop 5.10 (rd:central-formula, 980-1191)

general_results.label: Theorem 4.2 (rd:missing-vertex, 'The fixed-K missing-vertex implication')
general_results.statement: Verbatim: 'Fix the ring data E,K, with corank_{Z_2} Sel_{2^infty}(E/K)=1. Suppose binary families h_x = prod_{q in Q}(q*)^{lambda_q(x)} exist for arbitrarily large b, and for every nonzero x the product L(E^{(h_x)},s)L(E^{(h_x k)},s) has a simple zero and 2j_{h_x}-4w(h_x)-s(h_x)-s(h_x k) <= B with B independent of the family. Then ord_{s=1}(L(E,s)L(E^{(k)},s))=1. This implication does not assume Mordell--Weil rank one or finite Shafarevich--Tate group at the base.'
general_results.hypotheses: E(Q)[2] != 0; K split at 2N, nonexceptional; corank Sel_{2^infty}(E/K) = 1; all primes in Q good, odd, split in K; uniform bound B. Proof needs Prop 5.14 (bounded clearing factor), Lemma 5.17 (binary transfer), Cai-Shu-Tian explicit Gross-Zagier at conductor one.
general_results.relevance: none; K-RANK2: for the seed corank Sel_{2^infty}(E/K)=2 for every K (rank E(K) >= 2). Heegner hypothesis also fails for K=Q(sqrt-7).

general_results.label: Lemma 5.9 (rd:active-local, 'A ramified good odd place')
general_results.statement: Verbatim: 'Let F_v/Q_p be unramified, p != 2, and let T' = T_2(E) (x) chi, where E has good reduction and chi is ramified quadratic. Then H^0(F_v,T')=0, H^1(F_v,T') = E^chi(F_v)^_2, length_{Z_2} H^2(F_v,T') = dim_{F_2} E[2]^{Fr_v}. The quotient of the full local complex by the integral Kummer condition therefore contributes precisely this last length in degree two.'
general_results.hypotheses: Any E with good reduction at odd p; chi ramified quadratic; 2-adic coefficients.
general_results.relevance: none (2-adic local Tamagawa-type term at good twisted primes; the seed's open questions are at odd p and at bad primes).

general_results.label: Proposition 5.10 (rd:central-formula, 'The central determinant formula') incl. eq. rd:sha-comparison
general_results.statement: Verbatim: 'Suppose the product L(E^{(h)},s)L(E^{(hk)},s) has a simple zero at s=1. ... v(u_h(0)) = 2j_h - length_{Z_2} Sha(E^{(h)}/K)[2^infty] - 2 sum_{p|h} t_p + O_E(1) = 2j_h - s(h) - s(hk) - 4w(h) + O_{E,A}(1), omega(k) <= A.' Within the proof: 'length Sha(E^{(h)}/K)[2^infty] = s(h)+s(hk)+sum_{p|k} t_p + O_E(1)' derived from the Cassels-Tate isogeny identity (rd:isogeny-identity) for Res_{K/Q}E^{(h)} vs E^{(h)} x E^{(hk)}, 'This identity requires finite Shafarevich--Tate groups, as already established at these noncentral twists, but does not assume the BSD conjecture.'
general_results.hypotheses: Simple zero of the product (analytic ranks 1 and 0); Heegner hypothesis; extra-unit and CM fields excluded; 2-adic.
general_results.relevance: none for the seed (rank 2 over K). The Sha-comparison formula is a standard Cassels-Tate/isogeny-invariance consequence (Milne ADT I 7.3; DD2010 Sec 4.1) and is already available from the literature.

general_results.label: Proposition 6.1 (nv:local-witness, 'Local witnesses')
general_results.statement: Verbatim: 'Fix an elliptic curve A/Q and a nonempty filter of fundamental discriminants prime to 2N_A, with specified real sign and unit squareclasses at finitely many primes. If the root number in the filter is +1, it contains d of arbitrarily large absolute value with L(A^{(d)},1) != 0. If the root number is -1, it contains such d with L'(A^{(d)},1) != 0. Any additional finite set of primes may be excluded.'
general_results.hypotheses: ANY elliptic curve A/Q (modular); no rank or torsion hypothesis. Proof: self-contained first-moment asymptotics in a fixed progression mod H (8N_A | H) with Poisson summation (Lemma 6.3), quadratic large sieve (Heath-Brown 1995), Waldspurger nonnegativity, Gelbart-Jacquet symmetric square; derivative case adapts Iwaniec 1990.
general_results.relevance: marginal/cost reduction: NO. It is an existence theorem (no explicit d). For the seed the lab already has d=-7 with L(E^{-7},1) != 0. It could only serve to assert existence of alternative Heegner fields K (e.g. with prescribed splitting at 5843 for the plectic/FG route), but published theorems (Murty-Murty 1991, Bump-Friedberg-Hoffstein 1990, Ono-Skinner 1998, Waldspurger) already give this at a better grade.

general_results.label: Proposition 6.2 (nv:rough, 'Bounded-factor completion')
general_results.statement: Verbatim: 'There is an absolute integer A_0 with the following property. In the positive-root-number case of Proposition nv:local-witness, one can require omega(d) <= A_0 and require every prime divisor of d to exceed any fixed bound. The size threshold for the resulting d may depend on the curve, the filter, and the excluded primes; A_0 does not.'
general_results.hypotheses: Any A/Q; root number +1 in the filter. Proof: lower linear sieve (Friedlander-Iwaniec Thm 11.13) on the nonnegative sequence of central values (Waldspurger), after Hoffstein-Luo 1997.
general_results.relevance: none (A_0 not made explicit; the lab does not need bounded-factor twists).

general_results.label: Proposition 7.1 (co:even, 'Even coefficient system')
general_results.statement: Verbatim (abridged to the key clauses): 'Fix an even-sign filter and a nonvanishing index D_0 in it. There is a holomorphic cuspidal form g = sum a(n)q^n of weight 3/2, orthogonal to unary theta series, of level supported on a fixed enlargement of S, and characters eta, psi of 2-power order such that psi/eta = chi_{-sigma} and a(p^2 n) = (eta(p)a_p(E) - psi(p)(-n/p))a(n) - p eta(p)^2 a(n/p^2) (p not in S). ... For two nonzero squarefree coefficients, 2v(a(D)/a(D_0)) = v(L_*(sigma D)/L_*(sigma D_0)). Moreover a(D) != 0 exactly when L(E^{(sigma D)},1) != 0. Consequently any previously established bound v(L_*(sigma D)) >= 2w(D)+s(sigma D)-C gives v(a(D)) >= w(D)+(1/2)s(sigma D)-C_g.'
general_results.hypotheses: E with E(Q)[2] != 0 (section standing hypothesis); filter with fixed sign and unit squareclasses at S (S contains 2N); D/D_0 a unit square at every support prime. Imports Shimura 1973 (Hecke formula), Waldspurger 1981 Cor 2 pp.483-484 and Sec I.2 Prop 2 (with (H2) 'removed' by the paper's own argument), Ramsey 2006 (algebraic forms).
general_results.relevance: #Sha(E^{-7})[2^infty] only in principle: exact 2-adic valuation of ratios L_*(E^{(d)},1)/L_*(E^{(d_0)},1) is encoded in weight-3/2 coefficients. Not usable for the seed: computing a weight-3/2 form of level ~4N with N = 6.5e15 is far beyond the lab's budget, and the 2-part of Sha(E^{-7}) is not an open obligation (ORDER9 concerns p >= 5).

general_results.label: Lemma 7.3 (co:theta-bridge, 'Explicit weighted theta construction') with Lemma 7.2 (co:kummer)
general_results.statement: Verbatim: 'For l as in Lemma co:kummer, the reduced modular parametrization followed by lambda_M admits an integral weighted ternary theta lift. After extraction of the coefficients at multiples of |h_*| it gives a classical holomorphic weight-3/2 form g_M = sum a_M(n)q^n, of level supported on S cup {l}, with (co:recurrence) modulo 2^M. ... For squarefree admissible D, a_M(D) = c_0 2^{omega(N)} zeta_M(D) lambda_M(red_l(L P_D)) (mod 2^M), where zeta_M(D) is a 2-power root of unity and c_0, L are fixed integers independent of D,M,l. The extra index restriction at l is (D/l)=1.' Construction: B the definite quaternion algebra ramified at l and infinity, R an Eichler order of level N, supersingular set X = B^x \ B-hat^x / R-hat^x, Brandt eigenvalues a_p(E); Schwartz weights at 2, at p^e||N, at p|h_*, at l given explicitly.
general_results.hypotheses: E(Q)[2] != 0; fixed negative h_* with L(E^{(h_*)},1) != 0; good prime l with rho_T(Fr_l) = complex conjugation mod 2^M, (h_*/l)=-1, (D_w/l)=1 (Chebotarev); any level N including arbitrary 2-power (Jetchev-Kane Secs 1.1-1.2, 2.4-2.6; Cornut-Jetchev).
general_results.relevance: cost reduction: NO. This is a Brandt-matrix / supersingular-set construction at level N*l (class set size ~ N*l/12 * prod(1+1/p)), strictly larger than the seed-scale definite-quaternion enumeration (~5e14 classes) the lab already classifies as UNAFFORDABLE. The weights require 2^M-division points of Heegner points, not computable here.

general_results.label: Proposition 7.4 (co:odd, 'Odd coefficient detection')
general_results.statement: Verbatim: 'The forms in Lemma co:theta-bridge, after a fixed adjustment of precision, satisfy v(a_M(D)) >= min{M, j(P_D)-C}, v(a_M(D)) < M => j(P_D) <= v(a_M(D))+C. A visible coefficient detects a(E^{(D)})=1, and a fixed positive witness has bounded coefficient valuation as M -> infinity. All constants are independent of M,l,D.' Here P_D is the genus-character Heegner sum over K_D=Q(sqrt(D h_*)) and j(P_D) its index in the free line of E^{(D)}(Q).
general_results.hypotheses: As Lemma 7.3; Gross-Zagier for genus characters; L(E^{(h_*)},1) != 0.

general_results.label: Proposition 7.9 (co:symbol-interface) + Theorem 8.3 (gr:address, 'Address lemma') + Lemmas 8.1, 8.4-8.6
general_results.statement: Thm 8.3 (abridged verbatim): 'Suppose the binary symbols under consideration depend only on the arithmetic graph data and satisfy the contraction, whole-rational-prime omission, and primary-isolation rules of Proposition co:symbol-interface ... Fix b>=1 and either of the following terminal arrangements. (1) One symbol, a nonempty set of always active terminals, and a nonzero polynomial in their independent pair bits. (2) One or two symbols on terminals with nonzero linear activations ... Starting from any fixed realization of the terminal and stationary vertices, one can adjoin finitely many fresh primary auxiliary vertices, activated by nonzero linear forms, and choose only incidences involving these new vertices so that every symbol equals 1 at every x != 0.' Prop 7.9 gives the coefficient-level contraction rule: changing one oriented ramification bit at p in U changes the symbol by A((U \ {p}) cup {q'}), Fr_{q'} ~ g phi_p, 'unless p,q are both simple, in which case the change is zero.'
general_results.hypotheses: Purely combinatorial over F_2 (all-minors matrix-tree theorem, Chevalley-Warning) plus realization of residue-symbol prescriptions by Chebotarev/ray-class prime ideal theorem; Prop 7.9 is 'conditional on its coefficient lower bounds' (discharged by Prop 9.10 for the odd source).
general_results.relevance: none (combinatorics of quadratic-residue graphs à la Smith/Heath-Brown 2-Selmer methods, used only to engineer twist families).

general_results.label: Lemma 9.9 (pw:height-comparison, 'Height comparison')
general_results.statement: Verbatim: 'With the fixed modular parametrization and the fixed genus partner h_*, the explicit Gross--Zagier formula gives, whenever the relevant factors have analytic orders one and zero, 2j_h(k)-2j(P_h) = v(L_*(hk))+O(1). For k with bounded prime count as in Lemma pw:rough-companion, the error is uniform in h,k; for a fixed k it is uniform in h.'
general_results.hypotheses: Analytic orders (1,0) for E^{(h)}, E^{(hk)}; K=Q(sqrt k) split at 2N; extra-unit fields excluded; imports Cai-Shu-Tian 2014 Thm 1.1 (explicit Gross-Zagier with (N,D)=1, mu(N,D)=0).
general_results.relevance: none for the seed (rank-1 Gross-Zagier only; no rank-2 formula, so nothing for Q36).

general_results.label: Proposition 9.10 (pw:odd-lower, 'Uniform lower bound for the odd detector') with Lemma 9.8 (pw:rough-companion) and Prop 9.6 (pw:partitionable-even)

red_flags: Crux uniformity rests on a novel ultraproduct argument. The claim that all 2-adic constants are independent of the number of twisting primes and of the cube dimension (Thm 3.1, Cor 4.1, Prop 5.7 'Uniform residual valuation from outer rank reduction', Prop 5.14) is proved by contradiction inside an ultraproduct DVR O_infty = (prod_U O_j)/a of completed Iwasawa algebras with 'all-sequence evaluation' of cochain classes on products of Galois groups (Lemmas 4.4, 4.9-4.13, Prop 4.11). This replaces the residual-irreducibility input that standard Kolyvagin-system arguments need (unavailable at p=2 with rational 2-torsion). The manuscript itself repeatedly warns the argument is valid only for 'the same original stages and ultrafilter' and 'a single simultaneous construction' (Prop 5.7, Remark 5.18). This is unrefereed, nonstandard, and the single point of failure for the whole paper.

Prop 5.7 proof: outer cycles 'can be represented by vectors w_i for which v(D_i w_i) -> +infinity, without exact inner lifts', and rank-two evaluations of such approximate cycles are 'realized by inner derivative primes' by finite Chebotarev; then Lemma 5.3 'preserves each inner determinant valuation exactly' although 'its multiple of v_i has large valuation'. Whether the switch lemma (stated for genuine cycles with f(A)=v_0 != 0) applies to these approximate objects is asserted in prose, not verified.

Use of Kato at p=2 (cyclotomic.tex 329-330, 391-392, 429-435): the manuscript asserts Kato's trace/norm relations (Secs 8.9-8.12), Thm 9.7 and Thm 12.5(3) hold at the coefficient prime 2 without extra hypotheses, and that the only large-image input is Serre's open image. This must be checked against Kato's text; several Euler-system divisibility statements in the literature are formulated for odd p. Not verified here.

Prop 7.1 (Waldspurger comparison): the manuscript 'removes' Waldspurger's hypothesis (H2) and asserts 'No exceptional local representation at 2 is excluded by the same-local-class comparison' for arbitrary conductor at 2; the local theory of the Shimura correspondence at 2 is notoriously delicate and the justification is one paragraph.

Lemma 7.7 / Prop 7.9: the odd-source forms g_M are Hecke eigenforms only modulo 2^M (weights are 'any integer lifts' of values mod 2^M, 'need satisfy no characteristic-zero eigenrelation'), yet trace/determinant operators t(u), d(u) are defined via characteristic-zero eigensystems and Chebotarev continuity; the stabilization of minima and truth tables over M uses nonprincipal ultrafilters (Lemma 7.5, pointwise.tex 509-549). The passage between mod-2^M approximate eigenforms and characteristic-zero eigensystem identities is a subtle step treated briskly.

Prop 5.15 ('Assembly of the arithmetic diagrams') and Thm 4.14 are the load-bearing verifications that the actual Heegner/Selmer constructions satisfy the simultaneous-diagram hypotheses of Props 5.5, 5.7, 5.10, 5.14; their proofs are summaries ('Combine Lemmas ...', 'These are the three hypotheses of ...') rather than checks.

notes: Summary verdict for the lab: nothing in this manuscript proves or reduces the cost of any seed obligation (FIN, ORDER9, Q36, Sha[p^infty] at 3, 2243, 4547, 5843 or at good p, #Sha(E^{-7}), lemma TH). It is a pure p=2 result in the Selmer-corank-to-analytic-rank direction, applicable only to curves with s_2 in {0,1}; the seed has s_2(E)=2, and for E^{-7} its conclusion is already known. The published-literature imports it uses that are relevant to the lab's own chains (Cassels-Tate isogeny identity, Cai-Shu-Tian explicit Gross-Zagier, Monsky/DD parity, quadratic-twist nonvanishing) are better imported directly from their sources.
